label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
Rick, I need to say this straight, and I'd rather text it than blow up at you in front of everyone.

You told Gary Pruitt I'd list his house for 1% as a "family rate." I never said that to anybody. My listing rate is 2.5%, and I never agreed to 1% for him or anyone else. You offered my time and my number without asking me first.

On Saturday the 7th I pulled comps, drove up from north Phoenix to Chandler, did the walkthrough, and printed a full listing packet. That's about six hours plus the drive, and I did it because I thought this was a real deal for family. Sunday night Gary texted that he's going with ListLite for $3,995 flat. "No hard feelings." Fine, that's his call. But I lost a whole Saturday on a deal that was never going to be what you described, and when I called you about it you said "that's business, sis, can't win 'em all." That's not really the point, Rick.

This is the second time. Two years ago with your softball guy I let it go. I'm not doing that again. You don't get to look like the big shot with your friends while I do the work for nothing.

So here's what needs to change:

1. You don't give out my number without asking me first.
2. You don't quote my commission or any rate to anybody. Ever.
3. If someone wants to talk to me about selling, you ask me first, every time, and I decide whether I can take it.

Denise texted you this morning and you already gave her my cell. I'm not calling her. If you want to tell her I can't take her rental, that's on you. I'm not going to make it awkward for her, but I'm not doing free work because you promised it.

I'm not mad at Gary. I'm mad at you. I'm not trying to blow up Thanksgiving, and I'm still coming to your place. But I need you to hear this now so it doesn't happen again.

I'm happy to help family, Mom, your kids, anybody who needs advice. No charge on advice. That's not the issue. The issue is you offering my work like it's yours to give away.

Let me know you got this.

reasons: It says Denise texted Rick, but Rick texted the narrator about Denise.
